attacks.claim: Share links embed the owner's raw project API key as a query parameter, and the public share loader returns it to every viewer as replayKey. Anyone with the link, a crawler, a referrer, or a log reader gets a working credential for the paid project.

Deleting a share removes only the transcript row. The embedded project key remains valid, so the delete→404 QA check does not test revocation of the exposed credential, and the documented delete path cannot revoke it.
attacks.evidence: Shares can be deleted from Playground → History; deleted shares return 404. QA: Share link: create, open in incognito, re-run, delete → 404: pass.

attacks.claim: Rollback only toggles new signups and does not disable the share route, recall published share URLs, or invalidate keys already embedded in them. Once posted at 17:00 UTC the exposure cannot be undone by the documented rollback.
attacks.evidence: Rollback: `free_signup_open` off stops new signups; existing free keys keep working.

attacks.claim: The shipped free rate limit is 20 requests per second with burst 40 (up to 1,200/min), while the public changelog promises 20 per minute. QA validated a staging config with per: minute, so the shipped limit was never tested.
attacks.evidence: rate_limit: { requests: 20, per: second, burst: 40 } vs "Free accounts get **20 requests per minute**"; (staging config used `per: minute`)

attacks.claim: The $4k/month hard budget is not enforced. Two replicas are ~$3.6k/month (about 91% of budget) before scale-out, max_replicas 24 is roughly $43k/month at the same rate, and scaling is driven by queue depth rather than spend. No spend alert exists.
attacks.evidence: min_replicas: 2, max_replicas: 24, scale_on: queue_depth > 8 for 60s ... within the $4k/month free-tier budget

attacks.claim: The advertised 100k tokens/day free limit has no visible enforcement in the gateway diff: the free block sets no daily_tokens field (pro sets it to null), and max_tokens_per_request does not enforce a daily cap.
attacks.evidence: free: rate_limit: { requests: 20, per: second, burst: 40 }, max_tokens_per_request: 4096, pool: free-8b (no daily_tokens)

attacks.claim: Email-only, no-card signup with no per-IP, per-device, or global cap lets one operator create many accounts, each with a fresh free quota, draining the GPU budget and crowding out legitimate users.
attacks.evidence: Sign up with email, no card required. Free accounts get 20 requests per minute and 100k tokens per day

attacks.claim: Anonymous viewers replay against the owner's project quota, so a popular share on HN or X can bill the owner for public traffic they did not initiate, with no per-share limit or owner notice.
attacks.evidence: Viewers without an account replay against the owner's project quota.

attacks.claim: The '<30% utilization' capacity claim and the 1.2k tokens/request figure have no benchmark or load test for the 7B/8B models on H100, so the replica count and the budget conclusion are unsupported.
attacks.evidence: Two H100 replicas serve the projected free load at < 30% utilization

attacks.claim: Shares snapshot full message history with no expiry, retention limit, noindex, or warning before publishing, and the server-rendered OG pages make them publicly indexable and unfurled. Personal data pasted into a session becomes public.
attacks.evidence: messages: session.messages ... Share pages are server-rendered with Open Graph tags so links unfurl nicely on Slack/X.

attacks.claim: Alerting has no spend or budget alert and no key-abuse alert. A cost runaway or leaked-key misuse is unpaged, while ordinary scale-out past 6 replicas pages on-call.
attacks.evidence: Alerting: free pool replicas > 6 pages on-call; error rate > 2% pages on-call.

attacks.claim: The share feature has no flag and ships at the 16:00 deploy, 45 minutes before the signup flag, so key-bearing links can exist before any kill switch is active.
attacks.evidence: Deploy gateway config and playground at 16:00 UTC, flag `free_signup_open` on at 16:45 UTC.

attacks.claim: The 17:00 UTC public launch on blog, HN and X is irreversible and is scheduled before the key exposure, budget cap, and rate-limit mismatch are fixed. Those fixes should gate the launch.
attacks.evidence: Launch post: Wed 17:00 UTC (blog, HN, X)
